title: Fold-only re-bless invariance ('changed no more than the catalog fold explains') has no durable automated pin — only PR-prose splice proof
detail: Nothing durably tests fold-NEUTRALITY: existing pins prove a changed catalog_hash diverges, and gate 4 only checks new-golden-vs-new-data. I verified the property empirically (head code + base data reproduces all 32 base goldens, 32/32 green), but future re-blesses shifting beyond the fold would pass harness run silently.
recommended_fix: Add a fold-check: fixture pre-5.11 catalogs + base .t1 goldens under tools/ or goldens/_foldcheck/, plus a harness subcommand re-running pre-existing demos under fixture data; or a core test splicing a prior catalog_hash into a fresh dump and re-hashing.

title: PR fold-only proof cites tick-1 hash ab1fb0d04a90026c, which matches no committed golden — the committed previous boot tick-1 is 6c24e9cec592aece
evidence: head goldens/boot.t1:8 → "1 d1d2e53b7b1037ce"; base aec3c88 goldens/boot.t1:8 → "1 6c24e9cec592aece"; _bmad-output/pr-bodies/5.11.md:51 → "- **Fold-only proof (boot):** the tick-1 state dump under the final code, with the previous hash spliced at the fold position (bytes 33..40), FNV-hashes to the previous golden tick-1 **exactly** (`ab1fb0d04a90026c`); the un-spliced dump hashes to the blessed tick-1 (`d1d2e53b7b1037ce`). The era-0/no-demand shift is the fold alone." (git grep: ab1fb0d04a90026c appears ONLY in the PR body — no golden at head or base)
detail: The quoted 'previous golden tick-1' is unverifiable against the repo; the numbers document only the uncommitted intermediate fold hop (250679b1→17d3baf8) while the sentence concludes the whole-chain shift is fold-only. Property itself holds (verified), but the cause-chain citation is inconsistent.
recommended_fix: Restate the proof against the committed base: splicing 66c4324a06058860 at bytes 33..40 yields the base golden tick-1 6c24e9cec592aece (reproducible via head code + base data); or explicitly label ab1fb0d04a90026c as the intermediate 250679b1-fold tick-1.
